_comment: Canonical machine-readable index of Carlos Duarte's backtested trading strategies. Single source of truth for (a) the Trading_Index AI hub (full ledger, including failures) and (b) the LTCMA website Backtests page (docs/backtests.html, generated by ~/LTCMA/scripts/24_backtests.py). The website renders ONLY entries with "public": true (curated showcase of what worked); failures stay in this file as internal institutional memory. To register a new strategy: append an object and re-run that script (or the LTCMA daily refresh). Verdict/metric values are pulled verbatim from each backtest's REPORT.md; where a metric was not computed it is the string 'n/a' (never guessed). badge: green=Deployable (survives the full protocol and beats the S&P on risk-adjusted terms), yellow=Ensemble component (real edge, not standalone-worthy), red=Pass/no edge (failed cost-adjusted tests).
protocol: Optuna smart-search -> walk-forward + purged CV -> Deflated Sharpe (DSR) + PBO -> Monte Carlo 100k-500k -> post-2024 held-out -> S&P 500 gate -> survival bar (max DD < 10%). Cost model: pessimistic retail (FxPro embedded per-bar spread + markup + stop slippage). Sizing: 1% fixed-fractional (R-multiple, sizing-invariant Sharpe).

strategies.name: Buy-the-Dip / Sell-the-Rip
strategies.what_it_tests: Daily-timeframe pullback-in-uptrend (systemic alpha): buy dips while price is above a long trend filter, optionally short rips in downtrends. Universe: SPY/QQQ/DIA/IWM/EFA/EEM/EWW/GLD/SLV ETFs plus Gold/Silver spot, 2010-2026.
strategies.verdict_line: Robust but boring: 80-99% of the parameter space is positive-Calmar, so the edge is structural, not curve-fit. Deploy as a diversified SPY/QQQ/EFA ensemble (DSR 0.60-0.80, PBO 0.37-0.48), not a single name. Lead with the caveat: it is a low-drawdown S&P-replacement (~2x the S&P's Calmar at ~1/8 the drawdown), NOT a return amplifier - at a 10% DD budget it earns ~10.1% CAGR vs a de-levered S&P's ~3.6%.

key_metrics.headline_config: SPY flagship (DSR 0.80); robust survivors that beat S&P Calmar: EFA, QQQ, SPY. maxDD/CAGR shown @1% risk.

strategies.metrics_note: Metrics are the SPY selected config (highest DSR alongside QQQ). maxDD -4.3% and CAGR 2.9% are at 1% fixed-fractional risk (in cash most days); scaled to a 10% DD budget the SPY/QQQ/EFA ensemble earns ~10.1% CAGR. PBO range across instruments 0.37 (QQQ) to 0.85 (EWW). S&P full-window: CAGR 12.2%, maxDD -33.9%, Calmar 0.36.

strategies.name: Static SPY / IEF / GLD Diversification
strategies.what_it_tests: The deployable finding from the tactical-asset-allocation study: an equal-weight, low-turnover blend of US equity (SPY), 7-10y Treasuries (IEF) and gold (GLD), rebalanced monthly/quarterly, with an optional absolute-momentum cash filter. 2011-2026.
strategies.verdict_line: The momentum rotation didn't help - but the static equal-weight SPY/IEF/GLD blend beat every rotation variant tested: Sharpe 1.00, DSR 0.96, near-zero turnover, and it beats the S&P on Sharpe, Calmar and drawdown. Deploy as a low-cost diversified core (a 60/40-style -16.9% drawdown profile, not a sub-10%-DD product); the absolute-momentum filter is an optional crash overlay.

key_metrics.headline_config: Equal-weight SPY/IEF/GLD, monthly rebalance, turnover 0.35/yr; OOS (2025+) Sharpe 1.95

strategies.metrics_note: Highest-Sharpe, most timing-robust, lowest-turnover artifact in the entire TAA search (DSR 0.96 against ~1,200 effective trials). PBO 0.30 (full grid). MC maxDD 90% CI [-20.6%, -7.3%]. Benchmarks: SPY buy&hold CAGR 14.2%/Sharpe 0.87/maxDD -33.7%; 60/40 SPY/IEF CAGR 9.6%/Sharpe 0.98/maxDD -21.3%. The static blend beats SPY on Sharpe/Calmar/DD and ties 60/40.

strategies.name: Candle Range Theory (CRT) + Regime Filter
strategies.what_it_tests: ICT 3-candle range theory (C1 range -> C2 sweep+close-back-inside -> C3 reverse), gated by a daily 200-EMA trend filter on Gold. Tested vanilla and with regime overlays (trend alignment, ATR regime, day-of-week) on Gold, Silver, EURUSD, USDJPY. Span 2016 -> 2026-05-19.
strategies.verdict_line: CRT gated by a daily 200-EMA trend filter on Gold is a thin but real edge - PF 1.22, Sharpe 0.59, Calmar 0.33 - usable as one signal inside the regime-adaptive ensemble, never standalone. (Vanilla CRT, with no regime filter, had no post-cost edge - which is why this is an ensemble component, not a deployable system.)

key_metrics.headline_config: GOLD daily HTF, 3R target, + daily 200-EMA trend filter (507 trades, win 37%)

strategies.metrics_note: This report predates the full standing protocol: it used walk-forward IS (2016-2022) / OOS (2023-2026) but did NOT compute Deflated Sharpe or PBO, hence DSR/PBO = n/a.

strategies.name: Breedon & Ranaldo Local-Hours FX Rotation
strategies.what_it_tests: Published intraday FX pattern (SNB WP 2011-04): a currency tends to depreciate during its own country's trading hours and appreciate during foreign hours. Short/long each currency during its local session across EURUSD, USDJPY, GBPUSD, EURJPY, GBPJPY.
strategies.verdict_line: NOT DEPLOYABLE on any of the 5 pairs. The structural effect is real but tiny (EUR depreciates in Frankfurt morning) and smaller than realistic retail round-trip cost; every positive in-sample config fails DSR, held-out 2025+, Monte Carlo and the S&P gate. The intraday pattern appears largely decayed since its 2000s sample.

key_metrics.headline_config: EURUSD EUR-short, Frankfurt 10:00, 4h hold, ATR x2.5, news-skip (best of 5 pairs; still fails)

strategies.metrics_note: Metrics are the EURUSD leg (the only pair with positive full-period Sharpe); the other four are negative even in-sample. DSR 0.000 because raw SR 0.45 << noise-expected SR0 2.29 over 3000 trials. Held-out 2025+ Sharpe -0.45 (reverses). S&P bar: CAGR 11.91%, Sharpe 0.74, maxDD -33.92%.

strategies.name: Momentum Rotation TAA (rotation overlay)
strategies.what_it_tests: Antonacci/Faber-style tactical asset allocation: rank a pool of ETFs by trailing momentum, hold the top-N, with an absolute-momentum (trend) crash filter. Monthly/weekly/quarterly rebalance, 2011-2026. (The deployable byproduct - the static SPY/IEF/GLD blend - is catalogued separately as 'static_diversification'.)
strategies.verdict_line: PASS on rotation as standalone alpha. Relative momentum only helps in a broad pool with chronic laggards to avoid; in a tight good-diversifier pool it hurts. Nothing clears the <10% DD survival bar, and the best rotation's monthly headline is a month-end timing artifact (jitter blows DD to -36%). The only thing that survived deflation is plain diversification - see the 'static_diversification' entry.

key_metrics.headline_config: Pool A: 6m lookback, top-3/8, monthly, abs-mom filter (best genuine rotation; still fails survival bar + fragile)

strategies.metrics_note: Metrics are Pool A (best genuine rotation). DSR 0.91 is high only because the 216 grid configs are near-clones (mild deflation) - it means 'real positive-Sharpe portfolio', NOT 'rotation beats buy-and-hold'. PBO 0.30 full grid / 0.35 rotation subset. Run it weekly (not monthly) if deployed at all.
